immutable_origin.old_outputs: Verify the exact original141-file inventory and hashes before and after each whole job, including stale outer receipt and partial point14. Never overwrite, relocate, rename, delete, touch or repair an original file.
immutable_origin.path_resolution: A typed Julia continuation-path argument resolves only the original13 complete native123 folders to their actual original paths. Every other point/global folder resolves inside a fresh ignored run namespace. Add methods for this new argument type only; do not replace existing methods, monkey-patch globals, create filesystem aliases or rewrite receipts.
immutable_origin.partial_point14: Do not alias the partial folder. Recompute point14 from the beginning into a fresh real folder in the new namespace; retain every original partial operand and log.

immutable_origin.old_job_verification: Verify each reused job at its actual original canonical path, including original invocation, resources and a fresh separate Julia arithmetic audit. Aliased paths do not rewrite or counterfeit original receipts.

continuation.source_request: Use the exact original attempt2 request and source/build receipts. All132 source IDs, order, parameters, cuts, factors, uncertainties, target assumptions and refinement thresholds remain unchanged.

continuation.global_jobs: An explicitly bound adapter resolves old13 packets at their original paths and new packets at new paths. continuation.resources: Use the unchanged phase-specific whole-Julia-job time, command RSS and available-memory limits from the frozen policy. Cached reviews use the global limits. No limit or acceptance target may be relaxed.

continuation.failure: A failed, interrupted or occupied new job folder is retained and rejected. Never silently resume an individual Julia process, reuse its incomplete report, or recompute another attempt's completed jobs as this attempt's evidence. No automatic fitting follows this diagnostic.
continuation.origin_shutdown: An observation timeout is not a shutdown. Dispatch requires confirmed absence of the old owner; record boot/process identity and the immutable interruption evidence separately from job success.
